text: Git branching is an important part of version control. When you work on a project, you often need to add new features without breaking the main code. To do this, you can create a feature branch. This branch is a separate copy where you can make changes safely. Once your work is finished, you can merge the branch back into the main code. Many teams also use pull requests to review changes before merging. This helps everyone check the code and avoid mistakes. Following a clear workflow makes teamwork easier and keeps the project organized.
